predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: 'the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains' that the Byzantines ceded in the 681 treaty (Moesia, 'Bulgar conquest of Moesia' on the Asparukh page)

predecessors.name: Old Great Bulgaria
predecessors.text: Old Great Bulgaria's last Cliopatria shape (674-681, the Black Sea steppe north of the Danube delta) lies wholly inside the First Bulgarian Empire's first shape

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: the last Cliopatria shape (1015-1017), the remaining Bulgarian land from Ohrid and Bitola to the Albanian mountains: 'Bulgaria was annexed by the Byzantine Empire' in 1018 and became the theme of…

ledger.x: 681: Asparukh's Bulgars found the Bulgarian state between the Danube and the Balkan Mountains.
705: Tervel is rewarded with Zagore.

c. 805: Krum destroys the Avar Khaganate and takes its eastern lands. 'Around 805, Krum defeated the Avar Khaganate to destroy the remainder of the Avars' and 'advanced northward into the Tisza region'; the main page: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate', 'a border with…
809: Krum takes Serdica (Sofia).
812: Krum carries the war into Byzantine Thrace.
812: Develt and Mesembria fall to Krum.
813: Krum seizes Adrianople.
815: Adrianople is outside the new frontier.
815: Omurtag makes the thirty years' peace with Byzantium.

c. 825: Cliopatria's shape drops part of the Danube-Tisza lands in the west. Page silent on a loss: Omurtag page: 'In 818 the Slavic tribes of the Timocani, Abodrites, and Braničevci' rose against Bulgarian control in the west and sought Frankish backing; 824-826 diplomacy with the Franks failed. The shape change…
827: Omurtag's fleet on the Danube and the Drava recovers southeastern Pannonia.

c. 836: Philippopolis is incorporated under Malamir. 'the important city of Philippopolis (Plovdiv) was incorporated into the country.' The page gives no year; Omurtag died in 831 and Presian reigned from 836, so it falls in 831-836. The Omurtag page keeps Plovdiv outside the 815 border.
840: Cliopatria's shape drops the Slavonian and Pannonian land of 827-829.

Presian's conquest of Macedonia, placed at 850: the main page says 'the Bulgarians took most of Macedonia', 'the borders of the country reached the Adriatic Sea near Valona' and 'as far south as the Rhodopes and the plain surrounding Thessaloniki' with no year.
852: at his accession Boris I 'threatened the Byzantines with an invasion' but did not attack and 'received a small area in Strandzha'.
855-856: the Byzantines under Michael III and Bardas strike back.
864: Boris buys peace with his conversion.
893: the capital moves from Pliska to Preslav.
895: the Magyars, allied with Byzantium, invade Bulgaria.
896: Simeon, with Pecheneg allies, 'defeating them completely' at the Southern Buh; the Magyars left Etelkoz for the Carpathian Basin.
896: Cliopatria's shape drops the Black Sea steppe north of the Danube delta.
896: Bulgaria wins at Boulgarophygon (summer 896) and Byzantium pays tribute.
898: Cliopatria returns the steppe.
900: Cliopatria's shape drops the Bulgarian lands beyond the Danube and Tisza (Banat, Transylvania, the plain to the Tisza).
904: Byzantium cedes the Slavic lands round Thessalonica.
911: Cliopatria's shape adds central and northern Albania, the Raska uplands and Kosovo.
Late 913: Simeon is recognised as Emperor of the Bulgarians.
914: Simeon's war in Thrace.
917: Simeon takes the Serbian prince.
924: Serbia is annexed.
924: Bulgaria annexes Serbia.
926: Alogobotur invades Croatia.
27 May 927: Simeon dies in Preslav and the Croatian front ends with him; the page gives no Croatian treaty.
October 927: peace with Byzantium.
933: Caslav frees Serbia.
August 967 or 968: the Rus' cross the Danube.
970: Cliopatria's 970 shape no longer holds the land north of the Danube (Muntenia, Budjak, Bessarabia, Odessa).
971: John Tzimiskes annexes eastern Bulgaria.
Late July 971: the Rus' capitulate at Dorostolon.
972: the seat moves west to Skopje (infobox 'Preslav (893-968/972); Skopje (972-992)').

c. 980: Cliopatria's shape drops Oltenia and the Danube lands of the Iron Gates. Page silent on the year: the Peter I page says only that the Magyars' settlement north of the Danube led to 'the eventual loss of the region to the Magyars', which happened after Peter's death.
c. 980: Cliopatria's shape drops Syrmia (Srem) between the Sava and the Danube. Page silent: none of the pages opened mentions Belgrade or Syrmia after 971.
989: Samuel reaches the Adriatic.

c. 990: Samuel holds Thessaly and Epirus. The main page says only that he went on 'annexing the whole of Thessaly and Epirus' (no year); the Samuel page has Larissa blockaded 'from 977 to 983'. Year taken from Cliopatria's 990 shape.
991: Moesia comes back to the Bulgarians.
992: the seat moves from Skopje to Ohrid (infobox 'Ohrid (992-1015)'); the Samuel page: 'Samuel moved the capital from Skopje to Ohrid' without a year.
997: Samuel is proclaimed Emperor.
998: Samuel crushes Duklja.
c. 1000: Cliopatria's shape adds Syrmia. Page silent: the 998 campaign went 'northeast through Bosnia and Raska' but the page gives no annexation.
1000: Basil II's generals take the old capital.
1001: Basil II retakes Macedonia from Thessalonica.
1002: the final war.
1001-1002: Basil's campaign 'later reconquered Thessalian towns in 1001-1002.'
1003: Cliopatria's shape drops Epirus (Ipeiros).
1003: Vidin falls.
1004: Skopje.
1005: Dyrrhachium surrenders.

c. 1010: Cliopatria's shape drops the rest of Samuel's southern realm: the Vardar and Pelagonian Macedonia, Epirus in Albania and Pcinja. Page silent between 1005 and 1014: the Basil II page says only that 'Bulgaria fought on for four more years' after Kleidion; the Samuel page names no place for 1005-1013.
c. 1010: Cliopatria's shape hands the Iron Gates strip (Mehedinti) on the Danube to Hungary. Page silent; the Hungarian dossier counts the same cells as a gain in 1010 and withdraws them in 1015.
1015: Ohrid is taken and burned; Ivan Vladislav 'consolidated his positions in the mountains of Albania and Macedonia' and rebuilt Bitola from October 1015 (infobox 'Bitola (1015-1018)').
1015: Cliopatria's shape drops the Sofia basin, the upper Maritsa and the Danube plain from Vratsa to Lovech.
1018: the Bulgarian war ends.
1018: the last Bulgarian land passes to Basil II.
1018: the First Bulgarian Empire ends.

wars.name: Battle of Ongal and the Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 680-681
wars.outcome: Asparukh's Bulgars defeat Constantine IV's army at Ongal (680); in 681 the Byzantines sign a treaty ceding 'the territories to the north of the Balkan Mountains' and recognise the Bulgarian state.

wars.name: Tervel's campaigns and the treaty of 716
wars.outcome: Tervel restores Justinian II (705) and receives Zagore; 'Skirmishes continued until 716 when Khan Tervel signed an important agreement with Byzantium that defined the borders'.

wars.name: Campaigns of Constantine V against Bulgaria
wars.outcome: Nine Byzantine campaigns, 756-775; the pages opened record no change of border.

wars.name: Krum's war on the Avars
wars.outcome: The Avar Khaganate is destroyed ('Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'); Bulgaria borders the Franks on the middle Danube or the Tisza.

wars.name: Krum's war with Byzantium
wars.outcome: Krum wins the Struma valley (807), Serdica (809), Develt and Mesembria (812); Nikephoros I takes Pliska on 20 July 811 and is killed in the Varbitsa Pass (26 July); Versinikia 22 June 813 and the seizure of Adrianople; Omurtag's thirty-year peace of 815 fixes…

wars.name: Omurtag's Frankish war and the Pannonian campaigns
wars.outcome: After the 818 Slavic revolt and failed talks (824-826, ultimatum 826), Omurtag's fleet on the Danube and the Drava in 827 'restored Bulgarian control over portions of southeastern Pannonia'; 'Similar events took place again in 829 with the same result.'

wars.name: Bulgarian-Serbian war of 839-842
wars.outcome: 'Presian invaded Serbian territory in 839'; the three years' war ended with Vlastimir victorious, Presian 'driven out of Serbian territory'.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Serbia under Vladimir-Rasate
wars.outcome: Boris's son Vladimir-Rasate invaded Serbia; Mutimir's Serbs 'defeated the Bulgarians, capturing Vladimir and 12 boyars'.

wars.name: Frankish and Croatian war on Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'The Bulgarian-Slav campaign was a disaster, and Louis scored a great victory and invaded Bulgaria'; 'At the same time the Croats waged a war against the Bulgarians'; in 855 peace with Eastern Francia was restored.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Thrace
wars.outcome: Michael III and Bardas take 'Philippopolis (Plovdiv), the region of Zagora, and the ports around the Gulf of Burgas'.

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 863-864
wars.outcome: Michael III declares war in late 863; Boris sues for peace, promises conversion, receives Zagora back in 864.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Byzantine war of 894-896 with the Magyar invasion
wars.outcome: Over a trade dispute Simeon invades Byzantium; the Byzantines bring in the Magyars, who win in northern Dobruja (895); Simeon and the Pechenegs destroy them at the Southern Buh (896) and he annihilates the Byzantine army at Boulgarophygon; the peace brings…

wars.name: Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 913-927
wars.outcome: Simeon crowned emperor (913); Adrianople taken 914 and ceded back; Achelous (20 August 917); Katasyrtai; Thessaly to the Isthmus of Corinth (920-922); Pigae (922); truce on the Golden Horn (9 September 924); peace in October 927 confirming the existing…

wars.name: Bulgarian conquest of Serbia
wars.outcome: Petar Gojnikovic is taken to Bulgaria (917); 'Bulgaria annexed Serbia directly' in 924.

wars.name: Bulgarian-Croatian war of 926
wars.outcome: Alogobotur invades Croatia and Tomislav defeats the invasion; Bulgaria gains nothing.

wars.name: Rus' invasion of Bulgaria and John Tzimiskes' campaign
wars.outcome: Sviatoslav takes the Dobruja and 80 towns (968), Preslav and Boris II (969); Tzimiskes storms Preslav on 13 April 971 and the Rus' capitulate at Dorostolon in late July; eastern Bulgaria is annexed.

wars.name: Basil II's Sredets campaign and the Gates of Trajan
wars.outcome: Basil II besieges Sredets in 986 and withdraws when the Bulgarians burn his siege equipment; on 17 August 986 his army is 'ambushed and routed at the Trajan's Gates Pass'.

wars.name: Samuel's raid on Thessaly and the Peloponnese; Spercheios
wars.outcome: Samuel defeats the Byzantines at Thessaloniki, marches through Thessaly and 'entered the Peloponnese, devastating everything'; the Byzantines rout the Bulgarians at the Spercheios on 19 July 996 and Samuel is wounded.

wars.name: Samuel's Duklja campaign
wars.outcome: Samuel captures Jovan Vladimir and takes 'the Serb lands' (997, main page) or sends him to Prespa in a campaign through Dalmatia, Croatia, Bosnia and Raska (998, Samuel page).

wars.name: Basil II's conquest of Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 1002, a full-scale war broke out': Vidin (1003), Skopje (1004), Dyrrhachium (1005), Kleidion (29 July 1014), Samuel's death (6 October 1014), Ohrid (1015), Pernik (1016 siege failed), Ivan Vladislav killed at Dyrrhachium (February 1018); the nobility…

certainty.note: The Balkan-Mountains and Thracian frontier is approximate before the 815 line; the 716 agreement 'defined the borders' but the page names no line; the steppe frontier to the Dnieper is soft throughout and unverified before 803.

The Thracian frontier from Debeltos along the Erkesia trench to the Maritsa at Kalugerovo is a treaty line (815) and the Frankish frontier on the middle Danube is 'firmly settled' by 827, but the shapes keep the whole outline soft; the…
Only the 904 line 'some 20 kilometres north of Thessaloniki' is a stated frontier; the western, Serbian and Thracian fronts moved with the war.
The Byzantine frontier is the one 'restored to those defined in treaties of 897 and 904' in 927; the Serbian, Magyar and Pecheneg frontiers are approximate.
Rus' occupation, Byzantine annexation and Basil II's campaigns leave no stated lines; every frontier is approximate.
